info.name: Doctor 1 — Clinic Booking & Queue API — v1.0.0
info.description:
The complete v1 API, consumed by the Flutter app.

**This file is the source of truth.** The Postman collection is generated
from it (`php artisan api:postman`), and a test fails if a registered route
is missing here — so it cannot drift from the code.

## The envelope

Every response is one of three shapes, including 404s and 500s:

```
{ "status": "success", "message": "...", "data": { } }
{ "status": "error",   "message": "...", "error": { code, details, fields } }
```

Branch on `error.code` — a stable UPPER_SNAKE string — never on `message`,
which is localised prose meant to be shown to the user as-is.

## value + display

Anything rendered as text arrives pre-formatted, driven by
`Accept-Language`, so the client never re-implements Arabic formatting.
Use `value` for logic, show `display`.

## Clinic scope

The clinic comes from the token. **No endpoint accepts `clinic_id`.**
Another clinic's record returns 404, never its data.

A secretary may create one; any `price` she submits is silently ignored.
Full replacement, not a patch.

**Hides, never deletes** — bookings reference this row forever and carry
its snapshotted price and duration. Returns the updated record with
`is_active: false`.
Always all seven days, Saturday first, open or not.

Replaces the whole day — send every period you want kept. Period ids are
**not stable** across a save; never hold onto one. Closing a day drops
its periods whatever you send.

item.name: Start times for a day and visit type

request.description:
**The list changes with the visit type** — a 30-minute procedure offers
fewer start times than a 10-minute follow-up. Re-fetch whenever the
secretary changes the type.

Unavailable slots are **returned, not omitted**: render them greyed and
struck through.

Server-side rules: start times step by the clinic's `slot_step_minutes`;
a visit must *finish* inside its period; a slot is blocked by any
overlapping booking of any visit type; cancelled bookings free their
slot; touching intervals do not collide.

Call as soon as the phone is complete; `name` and `visit_type_id` are
optional so it can be called again as the form fills in.

Matching is on the **normalised phone only**, never the name — a typo
would otherwise split a patient's history.

The patient is created if the phone is new and reused if known — her ID
code is generated once and never changes.

`update_patient_name: true` replaces the stored name; without it a
differing name is ignored, so a typo cannot quietly rewrite the record.

`force: true` books anyway — past a taken slot, outside hours, or on a
closed day — and flags the booking `is_overbooked`.
One booking

Same body as create — a full replacement that re-runs the whole
availability check. The booking never conflicts with itself.

Editable while `booked` or `arrived` only. Changing the visit type
re-snapshots price and duration; changing the phone moves the booking to
a different patient.

query.description: Defaults to today in the clinic's timezone.

request.description:
**Already sorted — render in the order given:** with_doctor, then
arrived by check-in time, then booked by appointment, then done, then
cancelled.

The list re-sorts during the day: checking in moves a patient above
people booked earlier, and someone booked at 09:00 who arrives at 10:30
goes behind everyone already waiting. That is intended.

request.description: Keeps the secretary's place in a long list. It does not rebook anyone.
Today's `booked` + `arrived` — the multi-select behind "مريضات محددة".

Cancels the selected bookings with reason `emergency`, **frees their
slots**, and returns the call list.

**Nothing is messaged** — WhatsApp is v2. Omit `booking_ids` entirely
for "كل المريضات".

Reachable any time from the home-screen banner, which is driven by
`awaiting_rebooking_count` on the queue.

Phones are **unmasked** — every row has a call action. To take a patient
off this list, create a booking with `rebooking_for_booking_id` set.

query.description: Optional — an empty search lists everyone.

request.description:
Matches part of a name, the start of an ID code, or the last 4+ digits
of a phone.

**Phones are masked here** — there is no call action on a search result.

Summary plus every visit, newest first — **cancellations and no-shows
included**, each with its reason. A pattern of them is exactly what the
secretary wants to see.

The phone is **unmasked** here; this screen has a call action.

Three periods, each already compared against **the same span** of the
previous one: on the 8th, `this_month` covers 8 days and is compared
against the first 8 days of last month.

Counts completed visits only, at the price recorded when each was
booked. With fixed prices and no payment tracking in v1 this is
*expected* revenue, not cash collected — label the screen accordingly.

Cohort-based: the cohort is patients whose **first** completed visit
fell in the period, and the rate is how many came back.

`maturing_count` matters — a patient seen last week has not "never
returned", she just has not returned *yet*. Show it separately from
`first_visit_only_count` or the first month's number is meaningless.
